If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 2–5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract downward bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply (±0.50) in the last 3 days, apply a 3–7% correction to forecast at 15–30 day horizon, adjusting direction based on sentiment polarity.  
When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for late horizon (21–30 days) to prevent momentum overextension.  
If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, apply a 1–3% downward bias to forecast at 10–15 day horizon to reflect diminishing momentum.  
If sentiment is negative and price is near support, increase forecast by 3–6% for early horizon (1–5 days) to anticipate reversal or bounce.
